Create Derived Variables for Epidemiological Analysis

Source: R/sus_create_variables.R
sus_data_create_variables.Rd

Derives age groups, calendar variables and seasonal (climate) variables from standardized DATASUS data.

Usage

sus_data_create_variables(
  df,
  create_age_groups = TRUE,
  age_breaks = c(0, 5, 15, 60, Inf),
  age_labels = NULL,
  create_calendar_vars = TRUE,
  create_climate_vars = TRUE,
  climate_region = NULL,
  date_col = NULL,
  age_col = NULL,
  hemisphere = "south",
  backend = "arrow",
  lang = "pt",
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

df

A climasus_df (or tibble/data frame, Arrow dataset or DuckDB table) produced by the pipeline, standardized with sus_data_standardize(). Must have at least one row.

create_age_groups

Logical scalar, default TRUE. If TRUE, derives age_years (see Details for the 3-tier age logic) and the age-group variables:

  • age_group: factor from age_breaks/age_labels (cut(right = FALSE)).

  • Climate risk group (0-4 and 65+ "high risk", 5-64 "standard risk"): climate_risk_group (en), grupo_risco_climatico (pt), grupo_riesgo_climatico (es).

  • IBGE quinquennial groups 0-4, 5-9, ..., 75-79, 80+: ibge_age_group (en), faixa_etaria_ibge (pt), grupo_edad_ibge (es).

If age cannot be determined the function aborts with an error. With FALSE no age variable is created.

age_breaks

Numeric vector (at least 2 values, increasing; Inf allowed) of age-group breakpoints in years, e.g. c(0, 5, 15, 60, Inf) (default) gives 0-4, 5-14, 15-59, 60+; c(0, 18, 60, Inf) gives 3 groups. Intervals are closed on the left ([0,5)). Must be numeric, otherwise the function aborts.

age_labels

Character vector of length length(age_breaks) - 1, e.g. c("0-4", "5-14", "15-59", "60+"). NULL (default) generates labels from the breaks, in lang. A wrong length aborts.

create_calendar_vars

Logical scalar, default TRUE. If TRUE, creates calendar variables from date_col. If no date column can be found (and date_col was not supplied) the calendar variables are skipped with a warning. See Details for the variable set per backend.

create_climate_vars

Logical scalar, default TRUE. If TRUE, creates seasonal variables from the month; requires create_calendar_vars = TRUE (aborts otherwise, and also when no date column was found). Without climate_region: one astronomical season (astronomical_season / estacao_astronomica / estacion_astronomica), using hemisphere. With climate_region: a climatic season (climatic_season / estacao_climatica / estacion_climatica) and a dry/rainy season (dry_rainy_season / estacao_seca_chuvosa / estacion_seca_lluviosa).

climate_region

Character scalar or NULL (default). Brazilian climate region used for climatic seasons: "norte", "nordeste", "centro-oeste" (also "centro_oeste", "centrooeste", "Centro Oeste"), "sudeste", "sul". Case- and accent-insensitive; only the first element is used. NULL produces the astronomical season instead.

date_col

Character scalar, name of the date column used for the calendar and season variables. NULL (default) auto-detects it by system (e.g. data_internacao for SIH, data_obito for SIM, data_notificacao for SINAN, data_nascimento for SINASC, plus common names such as date/data/fecha and DT* columns). A supplied name that is not in df aborts.

age_col

Character scalar, name of an existing column with age in years. NULL (default) triggers auto-detection (see Details). If the name is not in df, a warning is shown and auto-detection is used.

hemisphere

Character scalar, "south" (default, Brazil) or "north"; defines the astronomical seasons. Other values abort.

backend

Character scalar, "arrow" (default) or "tibble". "arrow" processes Arrow/DuckDB inputs lazily (nothing is collected, except that decoding a composite DATASUS age code materialises the data) and falls back to "tibble" with a warning if it fails. "tibble" processes in memory. Any other value uses the tibble path.

lang

Character scalar, "pt" (default), "en" or "es". Language of messages, labels and of the names of the created variables; other values abort.

verbose

Logical scalar, default TRUE. Print progress messages.

Value

A climasus_df (tibble; lazy Arrow table/DuckDB table if the input was lazy) with the input columns plus the created variables. sus_meta: stage = "derive", type = "derive", system preserved, and a history entry added.

Details

Pipeline position: stage "stand" or later is required (run sus_data_standardize() first); the output has stage = "derive". Next steps: sus_data_aggregate(), sus_data_filter_demographics().

Supported systems: SIM, SINAN, SINASC, SIA and SIH-RD. The SIH sub-systems SIH-SP, SIH-RJ and SIH-ER and all CNES systems are blocked and abort early with an informative error (they lack age/date columns).

Age (age_years): age in completed years, resolved per row with a 3-tier logic (skipped if age_col is valid, or a direct age column such as age_years/idade_mae exists):

  1. Dates (gold standard): from the birth-date column (data_nascimento/birth_date/fecha_nacimiento/DTNASC) and the event-date column (e.g. data_internacao, data_obito, data_notificacao), as completed years. Negative or >120 ages become NA.

  2. Value + unit pair (per row, used where tier 1 is NA, or for all rows when no birth-date column exists): the age value (idade) plus its unit code (codigo_unidade_idade; raw IDADE + COD_IDADE). Units: 1 = hours and 2 = days (age 0), 3 = months (floor(value / 12)), 4 = years (value), 5 = 100+ years (value + 100). This is how SIH-RD gets its age, because it has no birth-date column. Implausible values (<0 or >120) become NA.

  3. Composite DATASUS code (fallback, e.g. SINAN NU_IDADE_N, codigo_idade): first digit is the unit (1 hours, 2 days, 3 months, 4 years, 5 100+) and the remaining digits the value, e.g. 4035 = 35 years, 5105 = 105 years.

Age groups are created only when create_age_groups = TRUE.

Calendar variables (when create_calendar_vars = TRUE; the date column is coerced with as.Date()):

  • In-memory (tibble) path, full set, names by lang: year, month, month name, day of week (Monday = 1), day-of-week name, day of year, quarter, epidemiological week, weekend flag, semester. Names: en year, month, month_name, day_of_week, day_of_week_name, day_of_year, quarter, epidemiological_week, is_weekend, semester; pt ano, mes, nome_mes, dia_semana, nome_dia_semana, dia_ano, trimestre, semana_epidemiologica, fim_semana, semestre; es anio, mes, nombre_mes, dia_semana, nombre_dia_semana, dia_anio, trimestre, semana_epidemiologica, fin_semana, semestre.

  • Arrow path (default backend, including in-memory input that is processed by it, and Arrow/DuckDB inputs): only ano, mes and trimestre (Portuguese names whatever lang is).

To get the full calendar set from an in-memory data frame use backend = "tibble".

Seasons (astronomical, by hemisphere): southern = Summer (Dec-Feb), Autumn (Mar-May), Winter (Jun-Aug), Spring (Sep-Nov); northern is the reverse.

See also

sus_data_standardize(), sus_data_aggregate(), sus_data_filter_demographics(), sus_data_filter_cid()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# SIM: age is already available
df_sim <- sus_data_import(uf = "SP", year = 2023, system = "SIM-DO") |>
  sus_data_clean_encoding() |>
  sus_data_standardize(lang = "en") |>
  sus_data_create_variables(
    age_breaks = c(0, 5, 65, Inf),
    age_labels = c("0-4", "5-64", "65+"),
    lang = "en"
  )

# SIH-RD: age from value + unit code (idade + codigo_unidade_idade)
df_sih <- sus_data_import(uf = "MG", year = 2023, month = 1:3,
                          system = "SIH-RD") |>
  sus_data_clean_encoding() |>
  sus_data_standardize(lang = "pt") |>
  sus_data_create_variables(
    age_breaks = c(0, 18, 60, Inf),
    age_labels = c("0-17", "18-59", "60+"),
    backend = "tibble"   # full calendar set
  )

# Seasons for the Amazon (Norte) region
df_n <- sus_data_create_variables(df_sih, climate_region = "norte")

# Only age variables
df_age <- sus_data_create_variables(
  df_sih, create_calendar_vars = FALSE, create_climate_vars = FALSE
)
} # }
